transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to waste your time, but... I've been having a little bit of trouble with my work lately. I'm a secondary school teacher, and, well, I love my job, I really do. It's just... when I sit down with a stack of essays or a new curriculum document, I fully intend to get right to it. 

But then, within, I don't know, ten minutes or so, I'll realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page. My mind is off thinking about three other things, and I'm barely taking in what’s right in front of me. I feel a bit silly even mentioning it, because maybe everyone gets like that when they're tired? I know teaching is demanding, and I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining. But it's been happening enough that it's slowing me down, and I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can to be a good teacher for my students. Is that... does that make sense for why I'd be here?
Do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety, especially when you're trying to focus on tasks like grading or planning lessons?

Oh, um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I'm actually pretty good at sitting still. I really don't want you to think I'm, you know, bouncing around or being disruptive or anything like that. 

When I sit down to grade at my desk, I stay in my chair just fine... it's really just that my mind kind of floats away, even though my body is perfectly still. I hope it's okay that I don't have that... that fidgety feeling? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not confusing things. Is it normal that I just sort of sit there quietly instead?
When you're trying to plan your lessons or organize your grading, do you find it hard to stay on track or get things set up in a way that feels manageable?

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little? But I really try my best to keep everything organized. I have all these folders and planners, and I always start out with a good system. I don't want you to think I'm just a mess or that I'm letting things pile up everywhere. I do get it done eventually. 

It's just, sometimes when I sit down to actually sort through the essays or map out the week, it feels a bit... overwhelming? Like I'm not sure which piece to tackle first, even though I know exactly what needs doing. I'll spend a lot of time just looking at the materials, trying to figure out the best way to arrange them. I usually manage to pull it together before the students need it, though. I hope that's the kind of thing you're asking? I just want to be helpful and make sure I'm answering correctly.
Do you often feel worried or anxious about how well you're performing your job, even when there's no clear reason to be concerned?

Um, no, I wouldn't really say so. I mean, I care a lot about my students, and I always want to do a good job for them, but I don't usually feel... anxious about my actual teaching. My principal actually gives me really positive evaluations most of the time. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging! I just don't want you to think I'm a nervous wreck or that I can't handle the pressure of the job. I feel pretty confident when I'm up in front of the classroom teaching the kids. It's really just that quiet desk work where my brain sort of... drifts off on me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay attentive in other areas of your life, like when you're reading a book, having a conversation, or trying to follow through on personal tasks at home?

Um, I think I'm mostly okay with those things? I mean, I really try to be a good listener when my friends or family are talking to me. I don't want you to think I'm ignoring people or being rude, because I really do care about what they're saying. 

Sometimes if it's a really long conversation or a super dense book, my mind might wander just a tiny bit, but I always catch myself and bring it right back. And with stuff at home, like chores, I definitely get them done. I mean, my house isn't perfectly spotless every single day, but I stay on top of the important things. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound like my whole life is a mess, because I really do try hard to keep things together. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Do you ever feel unusually tired or like you don’t have much energy, even if you’ve had enough rest?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I feel like I have a pretty normal amount of energy for a teacher? Teaching teenagers all day is naturally a bit tiring, but I don't feel unusually exhausted or anything like that. I always make sure to get a good night's sleep so I can be present for my students the next day. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm just dragging myself through the week or that I'm too tired to do my job properly. I definitely have the energy to keep up with the kids and get through my day. I mean, sometimes by Friday evening I'm ready to just relax on the couch, but I think that's pretty standard, right? I hope that answers your question? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the clearest picture possible.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with your mind wandering when you need to focus, and has it been happening consistently over time, even before your work got busier?

Um, well, I've always been a little bit of a daydreamer, I guess? But it really hasn't been a big issue until somewhat recently. I'd say it's been noticeably worse for about, um, 11 months maybe? 

It really only started getting harder when the school changed our curriculum calendar and added all these mandatory after-school planning meetings. It's just a lot more of that quiet, sit-and-plan type of work now, and that's when I struggle to keep my thoughts from drifting. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I can't handle a little extra work! I just think the shift in how much planning time we have is what brought it out. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you often find yourself forgetting things or losing items like pens, papers, or lesson materials when you're working on tasks at your desk?

Um, well... I guess I do misplace things sometimes? But I think everyone does, right? I really try to stay organized, I promise. It's just... well, I guess I do spend a little bit of time hunting for things I need for the day. Like my classroom keys, or my lesson notes... sometimes my USB drive. Oh, and the whistle and cards I use when I'm refereeing after school. 

It's silly, really, because sometimes I'm so sure I just had them in my hand like, five minutes earlier. But I always find them! I don't want you to think I'm losing important school documents or being irresponsible with my job. I usually just set them down somewhere and forget where that was for a second. That's pretty normal when you're juggling a lot of things, isn't it? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I really do try to keep track of everything. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt down, sad, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, even when things were going well at work or in your personal life?

Um, no, I don't think so. Not at all, really. I mean, sure, everyone has a frustrating day if a lesson completely flops or something, but... no, I've never felt hopeless or just sad all day like that. 

I actually consider myself a pretty positive person? I really love teaching and I'm very happy with my life, I promise. I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm, you know, depressed or ungrateful for what I have. Even with the extra planning meetings and everything, I still really enjoy what I do. I usually bounce back from stressful moments pretty quickly. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever feel an inner sense of restlessness or tension, even if you're sitting still, especially when you're trying to focus on work?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel tense or anything like that. I'm usually pretty relaxed, actually. 

I mean, sitting through those long planning meetings can be a little tedious, sure, and maybe I shift in my seat a bit, but I think anyone would after a while, right? It's not like I'm jumping out of my skin or feeling super anxious inside. I just... I might just need to stretch my legs occasionally. That's a pretty normal reaction to sitting in one place for too long, don't you think? I hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm, like, bouncing off the walls or something. I'm very calm, I promise. Does that answer your question?

This leaves F48.0 (Adult ADHD) and F90.0 (Childhood Hyperkinetic Disorder), with F48.0 being more likely given the adult onset and presentation.
